chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the flesh of wild animals that is gifted to a man, and he is given as a gift, and he does not know if it was hunted and he did not instruct with it, can he eat it? He said: No.
He said, And I asked him, Can the one in Ihram eat the cured meat of wild animals? He said: No.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim eat wild animal meat if it was gifted to him without him knowing it was hunted?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the meat of wild animals hunted by others and that hunted by the pilgrim himself, ruling that the latter is prohibited for consumption even if cured (qadid), reflecting the specific restrictions of Ihram. This narration highlights the Shia juristic principle that the prohibition extends to the meat itself when the hunter is in the sacred state, regardless of whether the recipient was aware of the hunt. The ruling underscores the sanctity of the Haram boundaries and the ritual purity required during pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the flesh of the wild animal gifted to the man, and he does not know it being hunted, and he did not instruct with it. Can he eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws, ‘Can the one in Ihraam eat the cured meat of the wild animal?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz ibn ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meat of wild animals given as gift, he does not know if it is hunted and he has not commanded it; if he can eat. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot eat it.’
I then asked about qadid (meat dried up in the sun) of wild animals for one in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot eat it.’”
